additional_concerns: Footnote 3 is anchored to both XML and prescribed-PDF submissions in u4.1003 and u5.1078. The extraction's absent-anchor uncertainty is resolved. Extending e-Cert to the web form or every resubmission would be unsupported.

The date-only candidate includes submissions before 9:00am on 2 February 2026. The source distinguishes the calendar-date channel rule, operational launch and blackout. Preserve competing interpretations of “following its implementation”; these temporal predicates are not equivalent.

The operational-launch candidates adopt an inclusive 9:00am boundary. The governing timezone and exact boundary interpretation remain unresolved; no supplied dependency ID identifies additional authority resolving them.

Direct contact during the blackout does not by itself establish an STR submission. Automatic migration likewise does not establish a new submission. Neither provision creates a general post-launch permission to use other channels.

Registration, schema conformity and e-Cert use are separate requirements, not stated prerequisites to the resubmission trigger. Their exclusion from these formulas does not establish overall submission compliance or authorize pruning the duties.

Actual submission appears in scope for some candidates but in the result for node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb. Nonfiling events can therefore yield OUT_OF_SCOPE versus FALSE; admissible event domains must be settled before treating the candidates as equivalent.

The history candidate delegates event quantification and completeness to an externally supplied Boolean. A false result requires sufficient history. Attribution to a report's responsible entity also needs examination when different entities submitted it.

These questions concern historical triggering, not whether a duty remains outstanding. A later STREAMS 2 resubmission must not erase the original trigger. TRUE_IS_SATISFIED must retain the typed meaning of trigger existence rather than compliance.

JFIU's promised resubmission guidance is absent and has no identifiable dependency mapping. It may clarify performance or discharge, but the source does not make its issuance a prerequisite to triggering the duty.

The XML provision also requires liaison to arrange a technical test. The extracted schema claim is supported as an atomic duty, but does not exhaust that provision. No available external dependency or overall executable correctness is established by these scoped checks.
